title: Protocol for direct measurement of stability and activity of mitochondria electron transport chain complex II
protocol: Prepare mitochondrial samples for calorimetric experiment.
Thaw all samples at 4°C for 15 min.
Transfer samples to calorimeter chamber.
Resuspend 100 μL of mitochondrial sample in 1.5 mL of mitochondria isolation buffer containing 1 mM ATP.
Place 20 μL of mitochondrial protein suspension into each enclosed chamber of the isothermal calorimeter (ITC).
Gradually increase heat in the calorimeter every 15 min until the sample reaches 37°C.
Inject 5 μL of succinate at a speed of 0.5 μL/s into the calorimeter in 7-min intervals.
Measure heat content reading following each injection of succinate.
Continue injecting 5 μL of succinate every 7 min until the heat content (ΔH) readings show minimal variation resembling a plateau.
Repeat measurements three times for all data points acquired.
Titrate succinate until the enthalpy (ΔH) remains unchanged, signifying full saturation of the enzyme.
Use software built into the calorimeter to calculate ΔH.
Repeat measurements three times for all data points acquired.
Calculate enthalpy (ΔH) for each interval by dividing power generated by the corresponding concentration.
Note that ΔH = ΔG – TΔS, where G is free energy, T is temperature, S is entropy, and H is enthalpy.
Once ΔH begins to plateau, Vmax has been reached, signifying full enzymatic saturation and consumption of available substrates within mitochondria.
At this point, the complex has reached peak stabilization in association with enzymatic saturation and succinate concentration.
Prepare calorimeter by adding a fixed 20 μl of mitochondrial sample to isothermal calorimeter.
Incubate at 37°C for 1 h.
Add 2 μL of 10 mM ATP into calorimeter.
Wait for 30 min following this addition and record enthalpy.
Titrate each time with 1 μL of 50 mM succinate into calorimeter.
Wait 2 min after each addition.
Document enthalpy of the reaction.
Continue titration until enthalpy is unchanged.
Pause point: If the reaction continually produces a positive value of ΔH, reassess necessary substrate concentration needed to reach stabilization.
Test combinations of substrates by removing and/or adding different compounds in steps 11 and 12.
Resulting ΔH measurement will signify the enzymatic requirement for stability.
Prepare samples for RIA identical to the conditions observed in steps 9–13.
Recall the number of titrations performed.
Determine the number of tubes to prepare, which is one more than the number of titrations.
Label tubes from 1 through Xn, where n equals the number of titrations plus 1.
Add 20 μL of mitochondrial sample to each labeled tube.
Independently add 1 μL of 50 mM succinate to each labeled tube.
Increase the amount of succinate added by 1 μL for each subsequent tube in correspondence with the total succinate titrated at each data point.
Label the first tube without succinate for data point "time 0".
Add 1 μL of succinate to the second labeled tube corresponding to the first calorimetry titration data point.
Add 2 μL of succinate to the third labeled tube corresponding to the third calorimetry data point.
Add 1-2 μL of 100 mM Trilostane to each independent tube immediately after adding succinate.
Transfer tubes to a 37°C water bath for 2 hours.
Centrifuge at 3,000 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C–8°C.
Collect the supernatant from each tube independently for RIA.
Use radioimmunoassay (RIA) protocol provided by MP Biomedicals to measure progesterone.
Maintain all samples on ice during metabolic reactions.
Allow sufficient time for scintillation vials to reduce static and minimize outliers in RIA counting.
Use supernatant obtained from step 19 for the RIA procedure to measure conversion of pregnenolone to progesterone.
